The authors would like to thank Samuel Petty and Michael Blunschi of the BTO Commercial Building Integration Program for their support in this work. The authors also acknowledge technical assistance from Tim Dyer and Joshua Standifer at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL). ix ABSTRACT The purpose of this Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA) was to test two rooftop commercial heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems supplied by Carrier Corporation to determine if they met the laboratory test requirements of the United States Department of Energy (DOE) Commercial Building HVAC Technology Challenge (hereafter noted as “the Challenge”). Results of the laboratory testing completed at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) demonstrated that the systems met all requirements of the Challenge.
